pages.text: The $(item)MoE Routing Rack$() deploys an $(item)Open-Weight Module$() from the training cluster. Put the weights into the rack’s Datacenter Hardware Hatch. The controller displays model residency, available memory and computation, and exposes the DeepThink setting.

pages.title: The 5×5×5 Stepped Structure
pages.text: The computer casing plinth carries energy and maintenance. Fit one $(item)Datacenter Hardware Hatch$() in an exposed casing cell for the weight module and four LoRA cards. The controller sits at (2, 1, 0). The rack uses the same compliant floor as the room, or an optional native receiver connected to the source room’s switch.

pages.title: Loading, OOM and Going Offline
pages.text: After a module is inserted the router asks the cluster pool for the TB the model declares:$(li)Pool is big enough → $(bold)ONLINE$(): the model is resident and bills CWU/t per tick.$(li)Pool is short → $(bold)OOM$(): the load is $(bold)refused$() and not a single CWU/t is charged.$(br2)$(bold)Pulling the card, pulling an HBM module, darkening a memory rack or a chunk reload$() all take the model offline on that very tick (EVICTED/EMPTY) — it never shows online while the memory is already gone.

pages.title: LoRA and DeepThink
pages.text: The Qwen deployment can reserve +4 TB per LoRA card, up to four cards in the hardware hatch. DeepThink is a controller setting. Family-specific effects on external machine settlements are scheduled for 0.6.3.

pages.title: Obtaining the Weights
pages.text: Feed a high-purity domain dataset into the training cluster import bus and collect the trained weights from its export bus. Install the module in slot 1 of the hardware hatch.
